<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. IX.|ACCORDING TO S. LVKE.|163}}</noinclude>shake of the dust also of your feete {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ A great fault to reiect the true preachers, or not to admit them into house for needful harbour and sustenance.}}∷ for a testimonie vpon them. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=6}}† And going forth they vvent a circuite from tovvne to tovvne euangelizing and curing euery vvhere.⊣

{{verse|chapter=9|verse=7}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 14, 1. Mar. 6, 14.''}}* Herod the Tetrarch heard al things that vvere done by him: and he staggered because it vvas said of some, That Iohn vvas risen from the dead. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=8}}† but of other some, That Elias hath appeared: and of others, that a Prophet one of the old ones vvas risen. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=9}}† And Herod said, Iohn I haue beheaded: but vvho is this of vvhom I heare such things? And he sought for to see him.

{{verse|chapter=9|verse=10}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 14, 13. Mar. 6, 31. Io. 6, 5.''}}* the Apostles being returned, reported to him vvhatsoeuer they did: and taking them he retired apart into a desert place, vvhich belongeth to Beth-saida. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=11}}† Which the multitudes vnderstanding, folovved him: & he receiued them, and spake to them of the kingdom of God, and them that had neede of cure he healed. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=12}}† And the day began to dravv towards an end. And the Tvvelue comming neere, said to him, Dimisse the multitudes, that going into tovvnes and villages here about, they may haue lodging, and finde meates: because here we are in a desert place. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=13}}† And he said to them, Giue you them to eate. But they said, We haue no more but fiue loaues and tvvo fishes: vnles perhaps vve should goe and bie meates for al this multitude. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=14}}† And there vvere men almost fiue thousand. And he said to his disciples, Make them sit dovvne by companies fiftie and fiftie. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=15}}† And so they did. And they made al sit dovvne. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=16}}† And taking the fiue loaues and the tvvo fishes, he looked vp vnto heauen, and {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''εὐλόγησεν αὐτοὺς:''}}∷ {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Here you see that he blessed the things, and not only gaue thanks to God. ''See Annot. Marci. c. 8, 7''.}}∷ blessed them: and he brake, and distributed to his disciples, for to set before the multitudes. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=17}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The miraculous prouidence. of God toward such as folow Christ into deserts, prisons, banishment, or whithersoeuer.}}∷ they did al eate, and had their fill. And there vvas taken vp that vvhich remained to them, tvvelue baskets of fragments.

{{verse|chapter=9|verse=18}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 16, 13. Mar. 8, 27.''}}* And it came to passe: vvhen he vvas alone praying, his disciples also vvere vvith him: and he asked them saying, VVhom doe the multitudes say that I am? {{verse|chapter=9|verse=19}}† But they ansvvered, and said, Iohn the Baptist: and some, Elias: but some, that one of the Prophets before time, is risen. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=20}}† And he said to them, But vvhom say ye that I am? Simon Peter ansvvering, said, The {{sc|Christ}} of God. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=21}}† But he rebuking them, commaunded that they should tell this to no man, {{verse|chapter=9|verse=22}}† saying, That the sonne of man must suffer many things, and be reiected of the Auncients and cheefe Priests and Scribes, and be killed, and the third day rise againe.<noinclude>{{rh||X ij|And}}</noinclude>
